horizon_note: 20 years matches the life of the plant the decision creates, and the LCOE difference already levelises that plant's capital over it; a 5-year count would be five years of a twenty-year mortgage with the asset kept. A shorter horizon makes self-supply look better, so 20 is conservative, and the annuity is bounded: counted for ever the penalty is only $68.5 B.
source: CoreWeave FY2024: revenue $1.915B, adjusted EBITDA ~$1.2B (62.7% margin), ~250 MW of active power at year end -> $1.915B/250/12 x 62.7% = $400,000 per MW-month of forgone earnings. Cross-checked against IREN FY26 results (27 Aug 2026), "Recent 3-year contracts >$20m revenue per MW (IT)", converted from IT to facility load at PUE 1.13; and CoreWeave Q2 2026 earnings call (11 Aug 2026), $2.58B quarterly revenue over 1.5 GW of active power, and $104B backlog against 3.7 GW contracted. All four carried at the FY2024 margin give $294k-$400k; the value used is the top of that spread. Adjusted EBITDA rather than revenue because a power delay defers the accelerator purchase rather than wasting it.
basis: forgone earnings of the whole facility while not energised, not depreciation of idle processors; accelerators obsolete on a fixed calendar so months lost at the front of life are not recovered at the back
